extracted.intended_audience: USPTO financial statement preparers, auditors, OMB/GAO reviewers, and other stakeholders in federal agency financial reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Accounting and disclosure policies used in preparing the USPTO Performance and Accountability Report, covering capitalization, revenue recognition, liabilities, benefits, leases, and funds from dedicated collections. Targets preparers and reviewers of USPTO financial statements and related disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property, plant, and equipment valuation and depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalized property, plant, and equipment are recorded at actual historical cost. Depreciation is expensed on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful life of the asset with the exception of leasehold improvements, which are depreciated over the remaining life of the lease or over the useful life of the improvement, whichever is shorter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As needed, useful lives of assets are updated to reflect current estimates; the estimated useful life is used on a prospective basis. Additional details are provided in Note 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of contractor costs for internal-use software
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor costs for developing custom internal use software are capitalized when incurred for the design, coding, and testing of the software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software in progress is not amortized until placed in service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expense recognition for non-capitalizable acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Property, plant, and equipment acquisitions that do not meet the capitalization criteria are expensed upon receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workers' Compensation accounting—billing and accrued liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims incurred for benefits under FECA for USPTO employees are administered by the Department of Labor (DOL) and are paid ultimately by the USPTO. The DOL bills the USPTO annually as its claims are paid, but payment on these bills is deferred approximately two years to allow for funding through the budget process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accrued Liability: DOL bills annually; payment deferred ~2 years. Actuarial Liability: DOL estimates future liability by applying actuarial procedures developed to estimate FECA benefits and includes expected liability for death, disability, medical, miscellaneous costs for approved cases, plus incurred but not reported claims. Actuarial liability is updated annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unemployment compensation billing and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees who lose their jobs through no fault of their own may receive unemployment compensation benefits under the program administered by the DOL. The DOL bills each agency quarterly as its claims are paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual, sick, and other leave accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual leave and compensatory time are accrued as earned, with the accrual being reduced when leave is taken. Sick leave and other types of non-vested leave are expensed as used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An adjustment is made each fiscal quarter to ensure that the balances in the accrued leave accounts reflect current pay rates. No portion of this liability has been obligated. To the extent current year funding is not available to pay for leave earned but not taken, funding will be obtained from future financing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee retirement systems and post-employment benefits recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees participate in either CSRS or FERS. The USPTO’s financial statements do not report CSRS or FERS assets, accumulated plan benefits, or liabilities applicable to its employees (those are OPM’s responsibility). The USPTO recognizes a funded expense for the USPTO’s share of costs and an imputed cost for OPM’s share of costs for pension, post-retirement health, and life insurance benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO’s appropriation requires full funding of the present costs, as determined by OPM, of post-retirement benefits (FEHB, FEGLI, pensions under CSRS). Any difference between OPM factors for funding and reporting purposes is recognized as an imputed cost. Additional details in Note 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrift Savings Plan and FICA contributions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees are eligible to contribute to a Thrift Savings Plan. For FERS participants a Thrift Savings Plan is automatically established and the USPTO makes a mandatory contribution equal to one percent of compensation and matching contributions ranging from one to four percent for employees who contribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No matching contributions are made to Thrift Savings Plans for employees participating in CSRS. Employees in FERS are also covered under FICA, for which the USPTO contributes a matching amount to the Social Security Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred revenue recognition and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferred revenue represents fees that have been received by the USPTO for requested services that have not been substantially completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two types recorded: (1) checks received with requests for services not yet deposited due to lag time between receipt and review; (2) fees for applications partially processed. The deferred revenue balance is calculated by analyzing the process for completing each service; the percent incomplete based on the inventory of pending work and completion status is applied to fee collections to estimate deferred revenue. Deferred revenue is largely impacted by changes in patent/trademark filings, first action pendency rates, and fee rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net position and cumulative results of operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Net Position is the residual difference between assets and liabilities, and is composed of Cumulative Results of Operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cumulative Results of Operations is the net result of the USPTO’s operations since inception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental cleanup liabilities disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO does not have any known liabilities for environmental cleanup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund Balance with Treasury classification and operating reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund Balance with Treasury is presented by Treasury fund type (Special Funds, General Funds, Deposit Funds) and by status (Obligated balance not yet disbursed; Unobligated balance available/unavailable; Temporarily not available pursuant to public law; Non-budgetary Fund Balance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO has been reserving a portion of annual appropriations to the Salaries and Expense fund as a designated operating reserve to smooth economic downturns and mitigate funding uncertainty. Specific reserve amounts and transfers (e.g., fee collections in excess of appropriations) are disclosed in Note 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounts receivable presentation and allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts receivable are presented separately for intragovernmental and with the public, with an allowance for uncollectible accounts applied to amounts with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables show gross receivables, allowance, and net receivables for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash presentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash disclosure includes deposits in transit and undeposited collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Totals reported and compared year-over-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of entity and non-entity assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-entity assets are amounts held on deposit for the convenience of USPTO customers (customer deposit accounts). Funds in customer deposit accounts are not available for USPTO use until an order is placed; once an order is placed the funds are reclassified to entity funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance sheet discloses intragovernmental customer deposit accounts and customer deposit accounts with the public and totals entity vs non-entity assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liabilities covered and not covered by budgetary resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO records liabilities likely to be paid as a direct result of events that have occurred. Liabilities covered by resources include realized budgetary resources, unrealized budgetary resources that become available without further Congressional action, and cash/Fund Balance with Treasury. Liabilities not covered include those requiring Congressional action before budgetary resources can be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realized budgetary resources include obligated balances and unobligated balances (operating reserve). Unrealized budgetary resources become available after October 1 once apportioned by OMB. Examples of liabilities not covered: Accrued Workers’ Compensation, Accrued Payroll and Benefits, Accrued Leave, Deferred Revenue, Actuarial FECA Liability, Contingent Liability. Disclosure includes tables of covered vs not covered liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FECA actuarial liability measurement and discounting
rubrics_metrics.description: The FECA actuarial liability is calculated annually by DOL as of September 30. Projected annual payments are discounted to present value based on averaging the Treasury’s Yield Curve for Treasury Nominal Coupon (TNC) issues for the current and prior four years to reflect average duration for income and medical payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest rate assumptions for discounting are provided separately for wage benefits and medical benefits (year 1 rate and thereafter rates shown for FY2016 and FY2015). The U.S. Department of Commerce estimated the USPTO’s liability based on information from DOL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating lease disclosure and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating leases (office space) are negotiated by GSA; leases are cancelable with appropriate notification and expire at various dates. Rent charges paid approximate commercial rental rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure includes future minimum lease payments by fiscal year and total future minimum lease payments, with descriptions of major leases (headquarters, Shirlington, regional offices) and their expiration/renewal schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments and contingencies disclosure standards
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO discloses routine administrative proceedings, legal actions, and claims, including threatened or pending litigation. Management assesses likelihood (probable, reasonably possible) and discloses estimated amounts when reasonably possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: management expects it is reasonably possible that ~$2,400 thousand may be owed for awards/damages involving labor relations claims; discusses when adverse outcomes were probable and resolution details. Payments to the Judgment Fund and existence/absence of major long-term commitments are disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment benefits expense recognition and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-employment benefit expenses are presented by category (CSRS, FERS, FEHB, FEGLI, FICA) and separated into Funded and Imputed components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Totals and comparisons for fiscal years are disclosed (e.g., Total Cost amounts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funds from dedicated collections—definition and use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds from dedicated collections are financed by specifically identified revenues required by statute to be used for designated activities, benefits, or purposes and must be accounted for separately from general revenues. At USPTO these include the Salaries and Expenses Fund, the Fee Reserve Fund, and the Surcharge Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-entity funds are excluded. The USPTO may use moneys from these accounts only as authorized by Congress via appropriations. The Fee Reserve Fund was established by statute (Leahy–Smith America Invents Act) to allow deposit of fees collected in excess of appropriated levels; access further requires annual appropriations. The Surcharge Fund was created by OBRA 1990 and is subject to statutory limits and Treasury warrant availability; lacking Congressional reauthorization the surcharge expired FY1998.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program cost composition and allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Program costs consist of both costs related directly to individual business lines (direct) and overall support costs allocated to the business lines (allocated). All costs are assigned to specific programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of program costs by cost category (personnel services and benefits; travel; rent, communications, and utilities; contractual services; depreciation; etc.) with direct, allocated, and total amounts presented for fiscal years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intragovernmental costs classification guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Intragovernmental expenses relate to the source of the goods or services, not the classification of the related revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intragovernmental costs and earned revenue are presented by Strategic Goal and business line, with net program income/cost computed accordingly.
